metric.why: Capex is the audited ground truth beneath every buildout headline. This site reads it directly from EDGAR company facts, quarterly, for the hyperscalers and the largest colocation operators.
metric.definition: Quarterly capital spending reported to the SEC by the companies building the facilities, tracked on this page from each company's own XBRL filings.

reading.body:
Hyperscaler and colocation capex is the direct measure of data center buildout velocity, sourced from audited SEC filings rather than press releases or analyst estimates.

Capital expenditure is the only metric that cannot be spun. When a company reports capex to shareholders and regulators, it has already spent the money on steel, concrete, power infrastructure, and equipment. This makes it the ground truth for tracking how fast the physical layer of AI is actually expanding. The hyperscalers and largest colocation operators drive nearly all U.S. data center construction, so their quarterly capex numbers show whether compute capacity is accelerating or flattening.

This data does not cover smaller operators, private facilities, or spending that falls below SEC reporting thresholds. It also does not break capex by geography, by AI-specific workloads versus other uses, or by what fraction goes to power and cooling versus computation hardware. Those details matter for understanding which regions are building out fastest or whether the grid constraint is biting differently in different places.

For tracking whether AI scaling is hitting infrastructure limits, capex trends are the earliest signal. If capex rises faster than power availability, buildings are being built without the power to fill them, and the grid becomes the chokepoint. If capex falls, the constraint has already won.
